featuredProjects.name: FormMate AI
featuredProjects.subtitle: Controlled AI form completion
featuredProjects.description: Talk your way through a long form once, then decide what actually gets submitted.
featuredProjects.longDescription: FormMate started from a small annoyance: retyping the same personal details into every application form on the internet. Paste the form's URL, talk through your information out loud or in text, and it drafts the answers. Nothing goes in until you've looked at it. Review-first was deliberate, not a limitation, since the moment a form-filler can submit without you checking, it stops being a productivity tool and starts being a spam tool.
featuredProjects.concept: Guided form completion that keeps you as the final reviewer.
featuredProjects.problem: The tenth time you type your name, email, and the same three-sentence bio into a form in one sitting is when you start abandoning forms instead of finishing them.
featuredProjects.solution: Give it a form URL and a conversational rundown of your information. It drafts field-by-field answers you can edit or regenerate, and the automation stops exactly where it would need your judgment instead of your data.
featuredProjects.currentStatus: The review-first workflow is built and defined in the repo.
featuredProjects.developerNotes: The version of this that worries me is the one that fills and submits without asking. I keep building the reviewed version anyway, because boring forms are exactly the kind of task where good AI assistance should be obvious and uncontroversial, and most of the industry keeps shipping the scary version instead of the boring good one.

featuredProjects.name: PasteVault
featuredProjects.subtitle: Private installable clipboard
featuredProjects.description: The clipboard that remembers you switched devices.
featuredProjects.longDescription: I got tired of messaging myself snippets of text just to move them from laptop to phone. PasteVault is what came out of that: an installable, searchable vault for text, code, links, and JSON that lives across devices without routing through a chat thread you weren't using for that.
featuredProjects.concept: A quiet cross-device home for snippets too useful to lose and too small to turn into documents.
featuredProjects.problem: Small, reusable text ends up scattered across chat threads to yourself, sticky notes, and half-remembered files, which makes it unsearchable and eventually untrustworthy.
featuredProjects.solution: Save structured snippets quickly, retrieve them with search, and keep sharing close to the item.
featuredProjects.currentStatus: Live, installable, and still getting regular updates.
featuredProjects.developerNotes: This is the project I'd actually use daily once sync and search are finished properly. Right now it's good for one device at a time, which is exactly half the point of a cross-device vault. Honest status: useful, not yet done.

featuredProjects.name: AI Agent Skills
featuredProjects.subtitle: Reusable agent workflow system
featuredProjects.description: The workflows I got tired of rebuilding from scratch.
featuredProjects.longDescription: AI Agent Skills isn't one product. It's the toolkit that came out of noticing I was solving the same handful of problems every time I started a new AI-assisted task: research, parsing, publishing, updating. It sits next to a few sibling repos that make up a small personal automation stack.
featuredProjects.concept: A personal operating layer that turns repeated agent tasks into specific, portable skills instead of one-off prompts.
featuredProjects.problem: Agent work gets reinvented every session if the useful patterns never get written down anywhere durable.
featuredProjects.solution: Package repeatable workflows as documented skills that can be invoked, audited, updated, and shared across projects.
featuredProjects.currentStatus: An active toolkit I add to and prune as real workflows demand it.
featuredProjects.developerNotes: The risk with any skill library is letting it turn into a junk drawer of half-documented ideas. I check this one against a simple test: would I actually reach for this skill next week, or did I write it because writing it felt productive. A few of the older ones fail that test and need pruning I haven't gotten to yet.

featuredProjects.name: Restore AI
featuredProjects.subtitle: Mobile image restoration app
featuredProjects.description: Old photos deserve a better repair shop than a dozen scattered tools.
featuredProjects.longDescription: Restore AI is a mobile concept for the moment you're trying to save a damaged or low-resolution photo that actually matters to someone: restoring, upscaling, recoloring, and resizing it without stitching together five different apps.
featuredProjects.concept: A focused mobile studio for improving old, damaged, or low-resolution images without exposing users to a technical editing stack.
featuredProjects.problem: Basic image repair usually needs several specialist tools, which makes a simple restoration job feel more technical than it should.
featuredProjects.solution: Bring the most common repair actions into one guided mobile flow, with a clear before-and-after review before export.
featuredProjects.currentStatus: The product foundation is defined; the mobile build is still ahead.
featuredProjects.developerNotes: This one stays a prototype because the honest version needs restoration quality good enough to trust with someone's actual family photos, running privately, at a cost that doesn't make the product pointless. I haven't solved that triangle yet.

highlightedProject.highlightTitle: This portfolio as a technical product
highlightedProject.highlightSummary: Project data, media previews, cursor states, routing, SEO, and build recovery all live in the same system. The portfolio functions as part of the actual product rather than packaging wrapped around it.
highlightNotes: Project records are data-driven, so the archive changes without touching page structure.
